Chapter 2: The Joy Principle—Deciding What to Keep
Here’s where things get interesting. At the heart of this method is a question that might seem simple at first glance—does this item spark joy?
This principle isn’t just a cute catchphrase. It’s actually your guiding light for every single decision you’ll make as you tidy up. Instead of just asking yourself if something’s practical, expensive, or a gift you feel obliged to keep, you’re invited to tune in to your gut. When you pick something up, or even just look at it, does it make you happy? Does it comfort or inspire you?
Now, if this feels a little strange, you’re not alone. Most of us hang on to things out of habit, guilt, or simply the fear of wasting something. Think about it—how many old sweaters, unread books, or awkward gifts are just hanging around your place, taking up space but not giving anything back?
The joy principle asks you to be honest with yourself, to put your own well-being ahead of what you think you should do, or what others might expect.
So, how do you actually do this? You start by picking up each item, one at a time. Really hold it. That physical connection matters—it’s your chance to notice how you feel. If what you’re holding gives you a little spark, makes you smile, or feels comforting, it deserves a spot in your life.
But if it doesn’t? It’s time to let it go. And here’s the thing—you don’t just toss it aside. Instead, acknowledge what it’s done for you, even if that’s just being there for a while. Saying a quiet thank you can make it so much easier to move on.
This isn’t about trimming down to some magic number or forcing yourself into minimalism. The real goal is to surround yourself only with things that really add something to your life. Maybe for you, that means keeping lots of books because you love each one. Or maybe it means letting go of most things except for a few truly special pieces.
Letting go can be tough, especially when objects are tied to memories, dreams, or relationships. That’s why it helps to treat the process gently and respectfully. Take a moment to appreciate an item’s role before you say goodbye.
And here’s where the joy principle goes even deeper. It’s not just for your stuff. As you tidy, you might notice you start applying this question—does it spark joy?—to other parts of your life. How you spend your time, who you spend it with, even the goals you chase. Suddenly, tidying up isn’t just about your home; it’s about living more intentionally and taking better care of yourself.
So, how do you put this into action? Here are the steps:
First, pick up each item and really notice how it makes you feel.
Next, keep only those things that truly spark joy or comfort.
For the rest, let them go with gratitude, and use this as a moment to reflect on your own values and priorities.
When you let joy guide what stays, tidying up shifts from being about giving things up, to celebrating the things that make your life richer.
In the end, you’re left with a home—and a life—that’s full of meaning, comfort, and real happiness.
